subject: Queueing fallback & SLA bridge proposal — Northfield
messages:
From: Alyssa Torres <alyssa@northfield.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@northfield.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2027 14:18:00 -0500
Subject: Dedicated capacity carveout request — throughput & queueing guarantees

Sean —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we discussed with Marissa on the call, Northfield is evaluating a Dedicated pool option for our inference workloads and we have a couple of hard constraints from engineering and procurement that will determine whether we can proceed this quarter. Quick summary of what we need to see in writing:

- Deterministic throughput guarantee for peak windows (we need a firm baseline for sustained tokens/sec for our tuned LLM).
- Reserved GPU count + minimum inflight tokens during preemption windows — we cannot accept long tail increases without compensating credits.
- Clear queueing behavior and tenant isolation so our low-latency requests are not impacted by noisy neighbor batch jobs.
- Burst behavior (how many tokens/seconds are allowed beyond committed throughput and for how long) and how that is priced.

Can you send a proposed carveout/addendum that covers the above? Procurement would like a written proposal by Dec 15 to hit our budgeting cycle. I’ve attached our Q3 traffic sample for reference (nf_traffic_profile_q3.csv).

Also note: legal will need to review any model-switching or fallback behavior — we cannot accept automatic model swaps that can materially change output without prior validation.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, Northfield AI
Alyssa@northfield.ai

Attachments: nf_traffic_profile_q3.csv (csv)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
To: Alyssa Torres <alyssa@northfield.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference, ben_carter@redwood.inference, laura_bennett@redwood.inference
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2027 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity carveout request — throughput & queueing guarantees

Alyssa —

Appreciate the clear list and the sample traffic. I’ve looped in Marissa (commercial) and Ben (runtime) so we can get a combined commercial+technical proposal back to you. Initial thoughts from the engineering side (high level):

- Dedicated pool sizing: we can reserve a pool sized to your sustained tokens/sec. For headroom we typically recommend an elastic buffer (10%–25%) depending on burst shape; we can be explicit about an "inflight headroom" metric to prevent sudden tail growth.
- Burst pool: we can attach a short-lived burst allowance (e.g., up to 30% of committed throughput for 60s windows) before overflow/backpressure kicks in; overflow will be rate-limited rather than silently failing.
- Queueing & tenant isolation: we support isolated priority queues for dedicated customers — that prevents batch tenants from preempting interactive lanes. We can document behavior for concurrency limits and KV cache priority.
- Preemption: for scheduled maintenance we provide 30-minute notice and automatic failover to a warm fallback model instance. Emergency preemptions would be rare but will be carved out; we can add notification webhooks for both.

For legal/commercial items: Marissa, can you draft a short SLA addendum (1–2 pages) with the above constraints and a couple of credit tiers? Ben, please flag any technical constraints that would prevent us from guaranteeing <200ms tail latency for controlled load patterns.

I’ve attached a quick sketch of the proposed queueing/fallback flow (sla_bridge_sketch_v1.pdf) as a starting point. We’ll iterate based on Northfield’s latency/traffic shape.

Next steps: Marissa to propose pricing and credit schedule, Ben to confirm feasibility and exact headroom numbers, then we send a formal addendum to procurement. If we can get their sign-off by Dec 15, we can meet Northfield’s budget window.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference

Attachments: sla_bridge_sketch_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity carveout request — throughput & queueing guarantees

Team —

Commercial perspective / constraints:

- Northfield is an ideal enterprise fit but their timeline is tight. We should aim for a 12-month committed reserve to make the numbers work.
- Proposed commercial outline (initial): 12-month commit, reserved equivalent of 8 A100-class GPUs, 10% elastic headroom included, additional burst beyond the included allowance billed at endpoint burst rates.
- SLA credits: propose tiered credits — if monthly availability <99.95% (service-level for the pool) then credit 10% of monthly committed spend; if throughput guarantees miss the baseline for more than two full peak windows in a month credit 15%. (We can refine wording.)

Ben — confirm the engineering feasibility of the 200ms tail and whether the proposed 10% headroom + 30% short burst is safe from an isolation perspective.

Laura — once Ben confirms, I’ll ask legal to draft the addendum for Northfield and push for an accelerated review. Also want to confirm whether model-switching controls need to be explicit acceptance clauses (they likely do).

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.inference
From: Alyssa Torres <alyssa@northfield.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@northfield.ai
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 10:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity carveout request — throughput & queueing guarantees

Thanks, Marissa / Sean —

A few clarifications from our side after reviewing your sketch and our SRE team’s review of the traffic sample:

- Latency SLO: we need 95th percentile tail <200ms for interactive requests during declared peak windows.
- Model switching: we can accept fallback variants only after a short validation window (we will provide validation prompts and acceptance criteria). Automatic switching without validation and a documented QA procedure is a non-starter.
- Preemption / notifications: we require webhook notifications for any runtime fallback/preemption events (real-time) and a monthly incident summary.

Procurement attached our standard questionnaire; please complete and return (procurement_questionnaire.pdf). Also please confirm whether the burst allowance is pooled across tenants or dedicated to our pool. We need the burst capacity to be effectively reserved to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

If you can provide a written addendum by Dec 12 that matches the above and outlines credit mechanics, our procurement team can fast-track.

Alyssa

Attachments: procurement_questionnaire.pdf (pdf)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
To: Alyssa Torres <alyssa@northfield.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference, ben_carter@redwood.inference, laura_bennett@redwood.inference
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Queueing fallback & SLA bridge proposal — Northfield

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clarifications. Attached is a concise addendum that captures the carveouts and guarantees we discussed: northfield_sla_addendum_v2.pdf. High-level summary of the proposal below so your procurement/legal teams have an easy checklist:

- Capacity & commit: reserved 8 A100-eq GPUs for a 12-month term (deal ID ND-2027-117).
- Headroom & burst: 10% elastic headroom for sustained smoothing; burst pool equal to 30% of committed throughput usable in 60s windows and reserved for your tenant (not pooled with other customers).
- Queueing & isolation: high-priority interactive queueing for your tenant, batch workloads on separate lanes; eviction/preemption limited to scheduled maintenance or operator-declared emergency.
- Preemption notices & telemetry: 30-minute scheduled maintenance notice; real-time webhook for any fallback/preemption events; monthly incident summary delivered to your SRE alias.
- Model fallback: automatic fallback allowed only to pre-approved model variants; any new fallback variant requires a short validation window and acceptance criteria signed off by Northfield.
- Latency & credits: Target: 95th percentile tail <200ms across declared peak windows. If target missed for two or more declared peak windows in a month, we propose a credit of 15% of committed monthly fees. If overall pool availability <99.95% in a month then 10% credit.

Next steps: Marissa will confirm the commercial schedule and update pricing; Laura will circulate the addendum to legal for redlines. If Northfield accepts the terms we’ll send a DocuSign for signature (link included).

We appreciate the level of detail — we want this to be predictable for your SREs and finance teams. I’ll wait for any redline feedback and will be available for a wrap-up call if helpful.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference

Attachments: northfield_sla_addendum_v2.pdf (pdf)
